title: Progression System
summary: Organizes account, character, equipment, skill, profession, mastery and regional progression while protecting accessibility and experimentation.

blocks.text: Progression in Symphony of Justice is divided into five connected layers:
Each layer represents a different form of growth.
The intention is to prevent all progression from collapsing into a single level bar.
Represents the player’s overall advancement through the game.
It does not directly determine how much damage a character deals.
Its main purpose is to track:
The final thematic name can be decided later.
The account layer should function primarily as an unlocking structure, not as a permanent progression wall.
LEVEL → ASCENSION/EVOLUTION → STATISTICS → MASTERY → TALENTS → SPECIALIZATION
Historical documentation already establishes that experience affects statistics and that growth should allow the player to give a character greater versatility.
Therefore, leveling improves the character’s base, while later systems modify how that character is played.
Weapons have their own progression independent from the character.
Historical documents already include separate experience materials for characters, weapons, and talents, as well as crafting tied to blacksmithing.
The goal is to allow a character to continue developing even if the player does not immediately obtain that character’s signature weapon.
A signature weapon should strengthen an identity, not unlock the character’s basic ability to function.
Skills have progression independent from the general character level.
This progression is mainly divided into:
Development of abilities associated with the character’s element.
Development of the character’s Ultimate ability.
Expansion of the character’s distinctive mechanic.
Improvements associated with what the character knows how to do and the utilities of that profession.
Later documentation already proposes three important divisions: Professional + Elemental + Personal / Unique Talent.
The Game Vision establishes that each region should contribute its own identity, enemies, resources, missions, and mechanics, and that the world can grow progressively through new areas and chapters.
Character Level represents basic statistical growth.
It should be the easiest form of progression to understand, but not the deepest.
Existing documentation already includes multiple sources of experience.
Characters are proposed to gain XP through two main paths.
Consumable items that provide large amounts of XP.
Historical documents explicitly mention books and experience upgrades for characters, including the possibility of producing them through blacksmithing.
Direct experience rewards playing with the character.
Materials allow newly acquired characters to be developed quickly.
Both should coexist, even if experienced players with large material reserves eventually rely more heavily on the second option.
The curve should begin quickly and slow down progressively.
The first ten levels should not require hours of play.
“Every major improvement requires a decision and an investment.”
However, this must remain marked as provisional: historical documentation does not establish a definitive numerical cap.
At certain level thresholds, a temporary cap can appear.

This provides a strong foundation for the system.

Early Evolutions can be more functional.
Later Evolutions can focus more heavily on optimization.
A newly acquired character must be playable immediately.
The player should not need to reach an advanced region before being able to move the character from level 1 to level 10.
This will be especially important for characters introduced through future content.
The skill system should allow the player not only to increase statistics, but also to learn and refine the character’s playstyle.
The documentation directly discusses Mastery as learning to command an elemental ability and improving both elemental and Ultimate capabilities through training.
Each character may have four primary progression lines:
The profession can provide a fifth line if the character has significant utility outside combat.
Profession Material — Associated with roles such as Doctor, Executioner, Summoner, and others.
Elemental Material — Associated with Cryo, Chaos, Spectrum, and other powers.
Special Drop — Obtained from bosses, Dungeons, or activities.
Existing documentation already mentions talent-related resources and activities among supplies and rewards.
A definitive number should not be locked yet.
This is where an important design decision is recommended.

The player should not be forced to “ruin” a character because they chose the wrong branch twenty hours earlier, for example by prioritizing an ability or section that later proves less important for that character.
“This character can only be played in one exact and static way.”
Historical documentation already envisions a tree composed of character evolution + weapon training + elemental ability + hidden talents.
That idea can be preserved and reorganized into three branches:
Utility, exploration, and characteristics associated with interaction with the world and Dungeons.
Application, reactions, and Skills focused on combat capability.
Unique Talent and individual playstyle, including normal attacks and passives.
These branches develop the same identity from different directions.
Account progression represents the player’s overall advancement and helps organize the gradual introduction of systems.
“You need level 47 because the game says so before you can continue the story.”
The Account Rank can progressively unlock:
Narrative progression should depend primarily on:
story + the player’s ability to complete the content, not on filling an arbitrary bar.
Opening new regions should be tied primarily to:
The player reaches the region because the story leads there.
The player finds a path or fulfills a requirement.
A recommended power level can exist, but it does not necessarily need to be an absolute wall.
The Game Vision already establishes that regions are connected to chapters and narrative expansion.
Account level may also allow higher world-difficulty tiers to unlock.
However, the player should be allowed to temporarily reduce difficulty if they become stuck, because this protects narrative progression.
The current sources do not provide concrete time targets.

I would not attempt to introduce everything at once.

“I just opened seven new menus and I do not know what any of them do.”

unlocked at least one additional system.
“I already have a team that feels like mine.”
An active player should be able to:
advance significantly through the first region;
The first week should open doors, not finish them.
Progression can be conceptually divided as follows:
Determines what content you can overcome: Bosses, challenges, reactions, execution, and mastery.
Determines how many options you have developed: more characters, weapons, materials, and exploration.
Determine where you choose to invest.
There should not be a situation where spending money can completely replace skill.
There should also not be a situation where skill becomes irrelevant because only the player who has farmed for the most months can win.
This area is barely designed in the historical documentation.
However, it will be essential if the project genuinely aims to receive content for years.
The historical vision already projected a long lifespan of approximately 6–8 years.
If that occurs, a player joining in year four cannot need four years to catch up with everyone else.
The time invested by veteran players should retain value without turning the time missed by new players into an impossible debt to repay.
As the level cap increases or content advances, early progression ranges can reduce:
Veterans already received the value of earlier access.
New players receive a less hostile entry point.

A character acquired through Gacha must be developable immediately to a functional level.

Free and starting characters must remain functional over the long term.

This is especially important for protecting new players.
